purpose: Complete the existing singleton-tie hypothesis on corrected QfO and supplementary Three Kingdoms after the prespecified OrthoBench pilot screen.
hypothesis: Deferring exact maximum-score singleton ties across distinct clusters removes an input-order-dependent attachment decision. It may reduce false merges, but it may also lose true orthologs; evaluate the complete metric vector without presuming improvement.
pilot_result: OrthoBench F1 fell from 0.7410607351873405 to 0.7365896292967041, a decline of 0.004471105890636373. This is a regression that narrowly passes the pre-existing 0.005 development follow-up screen, not equivalence or evidence of superiority.
pilot_gate: Job 24250 must be terminal COMPLETED with exit 0:0, both native/scoring arms independently admitted, and the independently recomputed OrthoBench F1 decline no greater than 0.005. Failure or larger decline rejects the follow-up, not the published method.
scientific_source: Use the immutable scientific source and original CPU libraries of the completed OrthoBench singleton pilot (1225e3f9b504ee68e90632bf4efdc92e8232703a, containing the singleton mechanism introduced at 9259e969ef3a600d38700365d2c00bb0d7215613). Do not incorporate later adaptive-coverage or kernel changes into this contrast.
inputs: Reuse the retained canonical whole-block accepted-hit checkpoints of job 24240. Do not rerun initial HMM searches or reorder rows within species-pair blocks.
control_gate: For each dataset reproduce the canonical candidate and constraint bytes, the three native biological products and rooted species tree before interpreting the variant. Revalidate retained control scores independently. Preserve the original failed QfO scoring attempt and its separate successful recovery.
control_scoring: QfO first_hit may reuse the independently verified recovered canonical assessment only after native product equivalence is proven. Do not rerun its unseeded FAS assessment merely to create a new control value. Score each variant in a new prevalidated short Darwin namespace. Three Kingdoms control scoring must reproduce the retained BUSCO-pair score.
fixed_parameters: CPM 0.1; Leiden seed 4; BLOSUM62; one profile pass; profile min_species 1; original profile-search settings; satellite_v2 candidate construction; species_overlap rooting; positive_paralogy pairs; inferred min_variance species tree; legacy support handling; high_confidence_pair satellite membership. Change only singleton policy at the initial and post-profile attachment stages.
selection: Combine these seven results with the independently admitted OrthoBench result. Use endpoint changes and Pareto tradeoffs, not a pooled mean. A decrease beyond 0.005 rejects a broad-default claim; passing this heuristic alone never establishes equivalence or justifies promotion.
execution: Run matched arms sequentially within each dataset, with control gates and explicit running rows written before every stage. Reuse compatible canonical tree caches. Require all gene IDs to remain represented. Validate source/runtime/library/scorer pins before and after execution. Do not modify or duplicate other running experiments.
limitations: All references are development-exposed. Cached downstream replays do not measure initial HMM candidate recovery or fresh pipeline runtime. Shared-host timings are confounded. FAS remains unseeded. TreeFam is supporting evidence and Three Kingdoms supplementary.
stopping: Run this fixed two-policy contrast once per dataset. Record failed or rejected arms, and do not retune ties, genes, or reference families after examining the results. No automatic default promotion.
